Introduction the Arohia Innovation Trailblazer Grant

If you’ve got a game changing idea that has the potential to inspire new ideas or create opportunities for other innovators, we’ve got you. The new Ārohia Innovation Trailblazer Grant is here to help you go far — then take innovation further.

Find out if the Ārohia Grant is right for your business: www.arohia.govt.nz

Māori business Paku on creating children’s toys through a Māori lens

Check out our latest video to hear from Dr. Johnson Witehira and James Prier, the masterminds behind Paku ltd, a Kiwi company that creates award-winning children's toys through a Māori lens.

Their unique kaupapa has earned them a spot as finalists in this year's Kamupene Māori o Te Tau - Māori Company of the Year Award of the prestigious NZ Hi-Tech Awards. We're proud to sponsor this year’s category in partnership with Poutama Trust.

Māori business AskNicely on making frontline work more rewarding

Check out our latest video to hear from CEO and Co-Founder Aaron Ward on human behaviour, the future of frontline work, and how a Māori worldview has shaped the rituals and practices of their business. 

AskNicely is a Finalist in this year’s Māori Company of the Year Award for the prestigious NZ Hi-Tech Awards. We're proud to sponsor this year’s category in partnership with Poutama Trust.

Māori business Envico Technologies on innovative technologies that are good for the environment

Recently we caught up with Kiwi Co-Founder Cameron Baker to find out how Envico Technologies are making their mark as Māori innovators - taking existing ecological knowledge with modern tech expertise to create lasting, multigenerational impact.

Envico is a Finalist in this year’s Māori Company of the Year Award for the prestigious NZ Hi-Tech Awards. We're proud to sponsor this year’s category in partnership with Poutama Trust.

Māori business Checkmate on getting your ideas off the ground

Straight out of Tauranga, innovative recruitment software platform Checkmate is a Finalist in this year’s Māori Company of the Year Award category for the prestigious NZ Hi-Tech Awards.

Traumatic incident response in education

Learn about Traumatic Incident teams, who can help schools and early learning services to prepare for, manage and respond to traumatic events, crisis and sensitive disclosures.

Learn more about traumatic incident response at Te Tāhuhu o Te Mātauranga | The Ministry of Education: www.education.govt.nz/school/health-safety-and-wellbeing/emergencies-and-traumatic-incidents/

Help lines
If you are a victim of family violence, sexual violence or there is someone that makes you fearful, threatens or harasses you, seek help as soon as possible. You have the right to be safe.

The Ministry of Justice has a detailed list of helplines available for people needing help: www.justice.govt.nz/about/news-and-media/covid-19-news/family-violence-and-sexual-violence-helplines/

Safe to Talk sexual harm helpline: 0800 044334, text: 4334, email: support@safetotalk.nz
Rape Crisis: 0800 88 33 00
Women's Refuge: 0800 733 843
Shine domestic abuse services free call: 0508 744 633 (24/7, Live Webchat is also available)
Hey Bro helpline - supporting men to be free from violence 0800 HeyBro (439 276)
Family violence information line to find out about local services or how to help someone else: 0800 456 450
Oranga Tamariki line for concerns about children and young people: 0508 326 459, email: contact@ot.govt.nz1737,
Need to talk? Free call or text: 1737 for mental health support from a trained counsellor
Youthline: 0800 376 633, free text: 234, email: talk@youthline.co.nz
Shakti - for migrant and refugee women - 0800 742 584 - 24 hours
Elder Abuse Helpline: 0800 32 668 65 - 24 hours, text: 5032, email: support@elderabuse.nz

Safer Online Services and Media Platforms Regulator

For more information on the discussion document or to submit feedback, visit the consultation webpage here https://www.dia.govt.nz/safer-online-services-media-platforms-consultation

Submissions close on 31 July 2023, NZDT.

ACC Progressive Procurement Process

ACC is breaking down the barriers to government procurement, so the process is simpler and more accessible for Māori health providers to tender for ACC’s contracts.

Te Puni Kōkiri and Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment are working together and have produced this case study to show ACC’s new regional approach to engaging with Māori suppliers.
